sourceIssues.locator: Corollary 3.2, published p.951, and its §11 uses, p.971; arXiv 1711.02189v3 pp.6,23. Published and v3 passages independently read; published p.951 image checked.
sourceIssues.printed: "Corollary 3.2. Let A ⊂ Ω × X be a closed, constructible complex analytic set that is Γ × {id}-invariant, and such that A ∩ (F × X) is definable. Then (q × id)(A) ⊂ X × X is a constructible algebraic subset. Proof. It follows from Corollary 2.3 as above." In §11: "Let V′_{n,ℓ} be the image of G(C) × id_ℓ(Ω̂) restricted to J^n_ℓ Ω, and V_{n,ℓ} its constructible algebraic (by Corollary 3.2) image in J^n_ℓ X", and likewise "an integrable algebraic (by Corollary 3.2) foliation".
sourceIssues.correction: Delete 'closed' from Corollary 3.2 and use its covering-space variant for J^n_ℓΩ→J^n_ℓX and their tangent spaces. If π is such a covering and A is saturated and constructible analytic with definable image B, then π(cl A)=cl B is closed analytic. Its image is definable, so Definable Chow makes cl B algebraic. The boundary cl A\A is saturated constructible analytic of smaller dimension and descends to cl B\B. Induct on dimension to obtain constructible algebraicity of B. Thus the intended generalization follows from the same closure-boundary induction as Corollary 2.3; no substantive missing properness theorem is needed.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed only after narrowing to a wording/statement slip, not the inherited substantive descent gap. The word 'closed' excludes the intended nonclosed input. But §2.1 makes q an unramified covering; for a saturated constructible analytic A, closure and boundary descend through this open covering. Induction on dimension, exactly as in the published proof of Corollary 2.3, shows that the definable image is constructible algebraic. The review gives this argument explicitly and applies it to the jet and tangent coverings used in §11. Reclassified gap/the proof to misprint/nothing and removed the demand for an unproved proper-image or finite-stratification theorem.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 11.1 proof, published p.969 / arXiv v3 p.22; published page image independently checked.
sourceIssues.printed: "We partition X_{d,d} into subsets X^i_{d,d} consisting of all pairs (φ, ψ) satisfying Stab φ_i = Stab φ_{i+1}, where φ_i denotes φ up to the i-th order, and i is the smallest such integer. Note that this is indeed a partition since each time Stab φ_i ≠ Stab φ_{i+1} the dimension of Stab φ_{i+1} is at least 1 smaller than that of Stab φ_i."
sourceIssues.correction: Supply a valid argument for finite-order determination and uniqueness. The assertion that every strict inclusion of jet stabilizers lowers dimension cannot be used as printed. One possibility would be to control component-group drops and the subsequent differential uniqueness step; another would be an independently established finite-order orbit theorem with all hypotheses verified. The existential lemma and the proposed bound m=dim G are not disproved by the finding, and no complete replacement proof is supplied here.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed the proof gap with an example inside the actual compact-dual geometry, not merely an abstract disconnected group. For G=PSp4(C) acting on the Lagrangian Grassmannian, the germ X(t)=tI+t³diag(1,0)+t⁴[[0,1],[1,0]] has third-jet stabilizer C2 and fourth-jet stabilizer 1; both have dimension zero. The review derives these groups from the fractional-linear action. Thus the strict-drop dimension assertion used on p.969 is false even here. This example does not disprove the existential lemma or the value m=dim G; a valid finite-order/uniqueness argument is still required. No unverified appeal to Scanlon is promoted to a proved repair.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 11.3 and proof, published p.971 / arXiv v3 pp.23–24; published page image independently checked.
sourceIssues.printed: "Theorem 11.3. Let k be a positive integer, r ≥ 2, and m as above. Consider a map (w, u, v) : Δ^k → Ω̂ × X × J^n_r X. If the image of (w, u, v) lands in V_{k,m} × V_{n,r} and the image of Tv lands in W_{n,r}, and if v restricts to u, then there exists g ∈ G(C) such that (w, u, v) = L(w, g, r)." Proof: "… Thus we may write g(t) = gn(t) for a function n(t) ∈ N. However, since v restricts to u, it follows that n(t) is the identity function."
sourceIssues.correction: Define the compatibility explicitly and include du=v₁∘dw (or full jet-chain-rule compatibility) in addition to the zeroth-order equality. Locally on a foliation leaf write v(t)=J_r(q∘g_0)(id_r(s(t))) for fixed g_0. Since q∘g_0 is a local biholomorphism, du=v₁ds and the added equation force ds=dw, hence s=w+c on a connected coordinate neighborhood. Absorb the constant translation τ_c∈N+(C) into g_0. This is the local missing step; any global formulation must retain its domain/lifting hypotheses. Merely asserting equality of zeroth-order values cannot replace it.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed the literal theorem under the zeroth-order interpretation of 'v restricts to u'. On a torsion-free modular curve, in a small disk with local coordinate t in the upper half-plane, let w(t)=2t, u(t)=q(t), v(t)=J_r q(id_r(t)), r≥3. The pair (w,u) is the translate associated to z↦z/2, and v follows the identity leaf; its zeroth-order value is u. If it were L(w,g,r), local lifting through the covering would force g(2t)=γt for one fixed γ∈Γ, hence the first derivative would be q′(t)/2, not q′(t). This derivation does not invoke Lemma 11.1 or Theorem 11.2. The review explains how du=v₁dw removes the ambiguity in leaf coordinates, while distinguishing that local repair from a complete re-proof of the global characterization.

sourceIssues.locator: §12.4, published pp.973–975 / arXiv v3 pp.26–27. The two invalid steps are on published p.974 (image checked). The differential input is Theorem 12.1 in print, numbered 12.3 in v3.
sourceIssues.printed: "On the other hand, since r has full rank, by our non-degeneracy assumption we may find a map φ : Ω → Δ^k such that (z, r, s, ...) ∘ φ is the identity, and thus the two fields are equal." and "(z, x, y) is a uniformized locus of rank k = rank(z) = dim U."
sourceIssues.correction: Replace the claimed inverse map by algebraic recovery from the invertible formal matrix r. At first order Dq(z)=Rr⁻¹; at order j, subtract the lower-order chain-rule terms and invert the induced action of r on Sym^j. This proves equality of the two fields. Put a=rank(z)=dim(z) when applying the differential Ax-Schanuel inequality, not a=dim U. The remaining formal coordinates contribute at least their analytic generic-fiber dimension to transcendence degree, giving the required final inequality. This repairs the indicated field/rank calculation, conditional on the stated differential Ax-Schanuel input.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed and reclassified to affect the proof: an independent proof elsewhere does not make an invalid step in this alternative proof harmless notation. An invertible formal jet matrix r is not the derivative of the base map z(t). For a modular curve take independent local parameters (a,b), b≠0, with z=a, r=b and higher input-jet coordinates zero. Then rank(z)=1 but dim U=2, even with open projection to X. The two fields are nevertheless equal by the triangular chain rule: q′=Rr⁻¹ and higher derivatives are recovered recursively. The final dimension argument needs dim(z), not dim U. The review writes the recursion and explains the generic-fiber dimension inequality. The theorem's independent §10 proof is not refuted.

sourceIssues.reason: Twice differentiating q_i(z(ε)) gives (Dq_i)D²z plus (D²q_i)(Dz,Dz). Thus the displayed term multiplying two first-order input-jet coordinates is a second partial derivative. The superscript 2 is visibly absent in both journal formulas and the corresponding v3 formulas. This is a notation slip, separate from E6's invalid inverse-map assertion.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 12.2, published p.975 / the theorem labelled 12.5 in arXiv v3 p.27; published page image checked.
sourceIssues.printed: The exception is stated as x contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X, although x=(x^(1),...,x^(ℓ))∈X^ℓ(K).
sourceIssues.correction: The exception is a proper weakly special subvariety of X^ℓ, with G^ℓ as the corresponding group for the product uniformization.
sourceIssues.reason: The whole statement concerns q^ℓ:Ω^ℓ→X^ℓ, and the tuple x is a point of X^ℓ, not X. Apply the preceding theorem to the product datum: dim(G^ℓ)=ℓ dim G, exactly the printed right-hand side. The proper weakly special exception belongs to that product. For ℓ>1 it includes relations between factors, such as the diagonal, not just exceptions inside one factor.
